description: A limbo bar for solid objects. Every round, the player in last place turns a hooded knob in secret, dropping a loose bar by 1, 2, or 3 mm, and then everyone commits a block from their own stock at the same instant, blind. Cups lift together; the tallest block that slides through without touching the bar wins the round and joins your score line, and a block that touches is gone for good. Nothing is marked and nothing is written down mid-round, the bar itself is the only judge. 2-4 players, 20 min, ages 14+. The complete rules ship with the files as RULES.md. By Bob.
prompt: 3D printed tabletop game Clearance: a printed gantry with a hooded threaded knob column, a loose bar resting in a clear lane, four player stock rails of unmarked square blocks in graduated heights, and four opaque commit cups, matte PLA parts on a wood table, studio product photography, 3/4 hero angle

story_blocks.body: The detent screw is 16 mm diameter and 118 mm long, threaded at a 2.0 mm pitch, with a 4-notch detent crown at its base. A quarter turn is one click; one click is exactly 0.5 mm of bar travel, felt and heard through the hood but invisible to the table. Travel runs 17.5 to 33.0 mm, 31 clicks end to end, and the crown holds each click crisp without letting the yoke's weight back-drive it.
story_blocks.lead: One click, 0.5 mm, and you never see it

story_blocks.body: The bar is a hollow 8 mm rod, 158 mm long, capped under 6 g, resting loose in two 4 mm V-saddles with nothing fastened. At that weight the lightest touch makes it rock or roll, so there is no judge to argue with and no call to make, either the bar moved or it did not. The saddles hold a 130 mm clear lane with nothing else in it.
story_blocks.lead: The bar is the only judge, it can't lie

story_blocks.body: The setter always turns eight clicks total: down 5 up 3, down 6 up 2, or down 7 up 1, so the bar always drops 2, 4, or 6 clicks, that is 1.0, 2.0, or 3.0 mm. The 78 mm knob hood swallows the whole hand so only the wrist shows, hiding which of the three patterns was used. Everyone hears eight clicks and sees the new gap; nobody but the setter knows where the turn reversed.
story_blocks.lead: Eight clicks hide the game's only secret

story_blocks.body: Blocks are 20 x 20 mm with height H drawn from a 42-rung ladder, 12.25 to 32.75 mm in 0.5 mm steps, held to +/-0.05 mm face to face. Bar heights sit on the 0.5 mm grid and block heights sit on that grid plus 0.25 mm, so a block is never exactly level with the bar, the smallest possible margin is 0.25 mm, and no ruler is in the room.
story_blocks.lead: 42 heights, always 0.25 mm off the bar

title: Clearance

use_case.body: Every round is two blind estimates at once: how far did the bar just drop, and which of my six blocks clears that but no more. You commit under a cup with everyone else, all four cups lift together, and the table watches the last block slide through clean or kiss the bar and get thrown out for good, out loud, with no judge but the rod itself.
use_case.label: Guess the gap, guess your own stock
